review.title: Claude Code's auto mode check was not sent
review.happened: Before running an action by itself, Claude Code asks a reviewer model whether to allow it. That request carried {{details}}, which your rules keep on this computer, so Latet did not send it.
review.happenedOthers: Before running an action by itself, Claude Code asks a reviewer model whether to allow it. That request carried {{others}}, which never goes to the reviewer, so Latet did not send it.
review.alsoOthers: It also carried {{others}}, which never goes to the reviewer.
review.meant: Claude Code did not run the action. It reports its reviewer as temporarily unavailable, and does not ask you: run the action yourself, or switch Claude Code to a permission mode that asks you. Your conversation was not touched.
review.todo: Leave it, and auto mode refuses the actions that need its reviewer. Or let {{details}} through to the reviewer, and auto mode works again: your secrets and personal data never go through.
review.todoOthers: Nothing to change: the reviewer never receives secrets or personal data, so auto mode refuses the actions that carry them. Run them yourself, or keep the secret out of your CLAUDE.md.
review.done: Done: from now on, the reviewer gets {{details}}.
review.surrogate: Or keep your real user name here: the reviewer is told the same fake user name the model sees, and only your user folder in paths goes through.
review.surrogateAllow: Use a fake user name, let the folder through
review.surrogateDone: Done: restart Claude Code (started with latet claude, or after latet agents apply claude) so it uses the fake user name.
review.surrogateNote: If your user folder has the same name as your user name, the reviewer still reads it in the paths.

plugin.todoUnmarked: Try the turn again. If it keeps stopping, the value reaches Claude Code by a way Latet does not mask: please open an issue. If the value is not sensitive, add it to the Allow list in Rules.

uninspected.todo: Take {{what}} out of the conversation, choose the balanced profile, or set images: mask in the project: images are then sent with the text in them masked.

projects.sources: Every rule of this list that applies in this project, each with where it comes from: your settings for the project, its latet.yaml, or your global rules, which are changed there.

data.title: Production data
data.description: Query results, API answers and logs the agent reads: tables, JSON and key=value pairs. Columns and keys named like secrets (password, api_key, *_token) are always masked.

strict.title: Strict data mode
strict.help: Every value of a table, a JSON document or key=value pairs in a tool's output is masked; column and key names stay. The same value always gets the same fake, so counts, groups and joins still work, and a query written with a fake runs with the real value. Files the agent reads and web pages are left alone, unless a rule below names them.
strict.switch: Mask every value of tool outputs
strict.profileHelp: As the profile: on with Max, off with Balanced and Secrets only. Strict or Normal stays as you set it, whatever the profile.

files.title: Files that count as data
files.help: Path patterns, with * for any characters: *.json, exports/**, .env*. A pattern without a slash names a file by its name. When the agent reads such a file, every value in it is masked, found by the file's format: JSON, tables (CSV, TSV), .env and properties, YAML. A markdown file only when a pattern names markdown (*.md), and then only its tables. This holds whether strict data mode is on or off. A pattern as broad as *.json also covers package.json: name the folders that hold data (exports/**).
files.empty: No file: the files the agent reads are left alone.

hosts.title: Web addresses that count as data
hosts.help: Host names, with * for any characters: api.internal.example.com, *.salesforce.com. A pattern for every subdomain, such as *.salesforce.com, also covers the domain itself. A page a web tool (WebFetch) fetches from such an address is masked as a tool's output: every value of its tables, JSON and key=value pairs. This holds whether strict data mode is on or off.
hosts.empty: No address: web pages are left alone.

tools.title: Tools and MCP servers that count as data
tools.help: Tool names, with * for any characters: mcp__postgres__* (every tool of the MCP server postgres), Bash. With strict data mode on and this list empty, every tool's output counts, except the tools that read files and the web tools (WebSearch, WebFetch), whose results are public content; with names here, only those tools' outputs count.

fields.title: Field rules
fields.help: The values of a column or a JSON key (a path like items[].sku; * matches any characters), masked as a type of your own, or kept in clear in strict data mode. Secret columns stay masked all the same.
fields.repoHelp: The values of a column or a JSON key (a path like items[].sku; * matches any characters), masked as a type of your own. Keeping a field in clear goes in each person's own settings.

images.help: Latet reads the text in screenshots on this computer and covers what it masks, once the text recognition models are installed. Send: images go out, masked when they can be read. Only masked: an image goes out only once its text was read and masked, and PDFs never. Don't send: no images or PDFs. The max profile sends none either, unless this says Only masked.

reviewer.title: Local reviewer
reviewer.description: A language model on your own server reads what the detectors left in clear, before it leaves, and masks what it finds. It runs on this machine, or on another of yours, and can add to what is masked, never take anything away.
reviewer.enabledHelp: Its server runs on this machine or on another of yours: llama.cpp, Ollama or LM Studio.
reviewer.sandbox: The tutorial's sandbox has no local reviewer: its server is outside the sandbox, and nothing here reaches outside it. On your own Latet, you set it up here.
reviewer.simulated: In the tutorial, the local reviewer is the Tutorial Reviewer: it is simulated, answers as the chapter is written, and reaches no server. Only your guidance can be changed here.
reviewer.urlHelp: Its OpenAI-compatible address, such as http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, and the model's id there.
reviewer.remoteHelp: It is on another machine, and Latet sends it the original texts, before they are masked. Use a server of yours only, reached over https outside your local network.
reviewer.httpsNeeded: Outside your local network the address must start with https://.
reviewer.inClear: Over http the original texts cross your network unencrypted. Give the server a certificate and use https://: a self-signed one is fine, trusted below.
